title: Split pea and parsnip stew with purple sprouting broccoli

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a plain whole food or cupboard staple, and vegetable stock counts as good stock.

supermarket.reason: Split peas, parsnips, purple sprouting broccoli and the spices are all everyday Tesco items at ordinary prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a knife, a board and one large lidded pan, and the technique is simple simmering.

works.reason: 1.2l stock plus a tin of tomatoes to only 250g split peas, simmered covered with little evaporation, leaves the 'stew' swimming like a thin soup, and the broccoli laid on top will sink rather than steam.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes is fair for slicing two onions, peeling and chunking three parsnips and rinsing the peas, and the 30, 25 and 6 minute simmers roughly match the 65 minutes of cooking printed.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including lemon and chilli, is used in the steps, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warming pulse and parsnip stew suits mid-January, and 250g of purple sprouting broccoli is a real vegetable portion rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are brief, clear and in plain British English, such as 'purple sprouting' and 'veg stock'.

hearty_healthy.reason: Split peas, parsnips and greens make a filling, protein-rich family dinner.
